findings.description: The spawn-then-end-turn model policy is vaguely scoped to a codex 'instructions/system-prompt overlay file - impl-located'. happy-cli already threads per-thread developerInstructions via startThread (runCodex.ts:1105 / codexAppServerClient.ts), so a default-off-gated developerInstruction append is the lowest-conflict home and avoids ANY codex upstream-canonical policy edit. Editing core/src/tools/handlers/shell_spec.rs widens patch surface despite an existing lower-conflict seam.
findings.resolution: US-002 retargeted to happy-cli: gated developerInstructions injection is the primary policy home; codex shell_spec.rs tool-description tweak demoted to documented LAST RESORT only. Codex cluster reduced to US-001 (the on_task_finished seam) alone.
findings.suggestedFix: Inject spawn-then-end-turn guidance via happy-cli developerInstructions gated by the new default-off setting; make the codex tool-description edit a true last resort.

findings.description: No targeted happy-cli tests required. Need explicit tests: default-off appends no extra -c (stdio AND ws spawn paths), opt-in appends the -c flags (both paths), unsolicited turn/started+turn/completed does not resolve a stale pendingTurnCompletion from sendTurnAndWait, and doctor reports readiness.
findings.resolution: Added AC8 enumerating required vitest cases across both stdio + ws spawn paths plus unsolicited-turn and doctor tests; US-003 and US-004 acceptance criteria now name these tests.
findings.suggestedFix: Add vitest cases for argv toggle (both paths), stale-promise non-resolution, and doctor readiness.

findings.description: Doctor 'policy in effect' has no concrete signal. codexDaemonDoctor.ts (via codexCommand.ts:18) inspects discovery records, ws health, lifecycle, RSS, version only. The probe can verify the happy toggle and spawned argv, but cannot prove an instruction-only model policy is active unless the plan specifies where the policy is stored and how doctor reads it.
findings.resolution: US-004 + AC7 now define a concrete doctor output contract: happy async-completion setting state; whether spawned app-server argv includes features.unified_exec=true and features.background_process_notification=true; whether UnifiedExec/ConPTY is actually active (exec_command model-visible); whether the async-completion developerInstruction is present; and a human-readable reason when async completion will NOT fire.
findings.suggestedFix: Define a structured doctor readiness contract reading the setting, the spawned argv, UnifiedExec/ConPTY state, and the injected developer instruction.

findings.description: AC5 'byte-for-byte unchanged' is not realistically testable for live app-server sessions (timestamps/ids) and too broad.
findings.resolution: AC5 rewritten as observable invariants: setting omitted -> disabled; no -c features.unified_exec / features.background_process_notification in spawned argv (both stdio+ws); no async-completion developerInstruction appended; no bg-completion consumer active; existing argv + turn-completion unit tests remain green.

findings.description: AC4 'deliberate, documented ordering' for two concurrent exits + operator message does not state the intended order, and ignores that codex coalesces adjacent background notifications into one <task_notification> (tasks/mod.rs:115-139, :171-189).
findings.resolution: AC4 now specifies: the active operator turn completes first; then queued background notifications start ONE synthetic turn, coalesced when adjacent; covered by a codex unit/integration test. Enqueue-order semantics for multiple completions stated.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the inferred order the contract and require a test; account for coalescing.

findings.description: LOW-B as described is not implementable: happy-cli's exec_command_end mapping (codexAppServerClient.ts:583) only emits type/call_id/output/exit_code/duration_ms/status/cwd/command and drops process_id/source, which codex protocol DOES carry on ExecCommandEndEvent (protocol.rs:3067). Without preserving those, foreground vs background completion cannot be discriminated, so AC3 cannot be verified for the LOW-B path.
findings.resolution: US-006 now has a mandatory first sub-task: define the background/subscribed discriminator by preserving process_id/source through the happy-cli exec_command_end mapping, before building the consumer. AC3 reworded so the LOW-B negative case is gated on that discriminator; under LOW-A, AC3 holds because codex only wakes via the watcher path.
findings.suggestedFix: Define discriminator + mapping change as US-006 step 1.

findings.description: Enablement omits the UnifiedExec prerequisite. On Windows Feature::UnifiedExec defaults off (features/src/lib.rs:735-745) and the exec_command/write_stdin/await_background_completion tools are ONLY registered under ConfigShellToolType::UnifiedExec (spec_plan.rs:542-552); tool selection falls back to ShellCommand unless UnifiedExec is enabled and ConPTY supported (tool_config.rs:60-80). So background_process_notification can be 'on' yet the watcher path is unreachable and the feature silently fails.
findings.resolution: US-003 enablement now passes/verifies BOTH -c features.unified_exec=true and -c features.background_process_notification=true; doctor (US-004) fails loudly unless UnifiedExec is actually active and exec_command is model-visible. AC1 and AC7 updated to require the UnifiedExec prerequisite.
findings.suggestedFix: Enable+verify UnifiedExec alongside the bg-notification flag; doctor checks ConPTY/UnifiedExec active.

findings.description: LOW-A can hang when an operator message arrives while an unsolicited completion turn is active. The client only creates pendingTurnCompletion for sendTurnAndWait (codexAppServerClient.ts:265-271). An unsolicited codex turn S sets _turnId via task_started (:2238-2244) but has no pending promise; a concurrent user sendTurnAndWait captures ignoredTurnId=S and waits for a new turn U, but core may steer the user input into the already-active turn S (session/mod.rs:3194-3255), so completion for S is ignored (:1776-1794) and U never completes -> 10-minute timeout (:1912-1913).
findings.resolution: US-003 now mandates explicit unsolicited-active-turn tracking: before sendTurnAndWait, if _turnId is active with no pendingTurnCompletion, either wait for the unsolicited turn to complete before dispatching the queued user message, or steer and wait on the active turn id. AC1 adds a live/test case: operator message sent WHILE the unsolicited completion turn is active must not hang.
findings.suggestedFix: Track unsolicited active turns and serialize/steer the next user message; add a test.

findings.sectionRef: Approach > Codex race-proof seam / US-001 / AC2
findings.description: The on_task_finished insertion point is ambiguous enough to no-op. The first active_turn lock drops at tasks/mod.rs:692-699 and pending input drains at :703-736, but active_turn is only cleared at :888-899; maybe_start_turn_for_pending_work returns immediately if active_turn.is_some() (:580-584). Inserting after ~736 will never deadlock but will ALWAYS no-op, leaving the race unfixed.
findings.resolution: US-001 now specifies the seam goes AFTER active_turn is cleared (~:888-899) and after the MaybeContinueIfIdle apply path (~:900-908), NOT after the pending-input drain. This reconciles the earlier line-number divergence (888-899 is the correct anchor). The regression test must fail if the wake is attempted before active_turn is cleared. No infinite-loop risk confirmed (helper returns on empty queues :571-578; start_task drains queued items :443-450).
findings.suggestedFix: Place the feature-gated re-check after active_turn is cleared / after MaybeContinueIfIdle apply; assert placement in the test.

findings.sectionRef: Approach > Codex model policy / US-002 / Open Questions
findings.description: 'Do not call await_background_completion' conflicts with the minimal payload. The notification carries only process_id + exit_code (async_watcher.rs:185-198), not the transcript; the existing way to retrieve aggregated output is await_background_completion (process_manager.rs:755-830). The agent may wake with no actionable result.
findings.resolution: US-002 policy refined: forbid PRE-exit blocking awaits / polls (which suppress the watcher), but explicitly ALLOW a POST-notification, already-exited retrieval call when the model needs output (post-exit await returns the transcript; the dedup CAS has already fired so it does not double-notify). Open Question 2 updated.
findings.suggestedFix: Permit post-notification retrieval; forbid only pre-end-turn blocking awaits.

findings.description: Dedup suppression is broader than 'await + empty poll'. Any write_stdin path that observes exit can claim the flag (process_manager.rs:677-679), and unconditional exited-state stores also suppress (:722-724, :807-808). A non-empty stdin write racing with exit can suppress the watcher.
findings.resolution: US-002 policy broadened: after spawning a subscribed fire-and-forget process, avoid ALL follow-up write_stdin/await interactions (not just empty polls) unless intentionally taking over completion handling.
findings.suggestedFix: State 'avoid all follow-up write_stdin/await after fire-and-forget spawn'.

findings.description: 'Implement LOW-B only if LOW-A does not surface cleanly' is too hand-wavy for Ralph execution; a member could skip US-006 without evidence or build it prematurely.
findings.resolution: US-005 now produces a structured validation decision artifact (.ralph/jobs/<job>/low-a-validation.json) with explicit fields: unsolicitedTurnRendered, stalePromiseObserved, operatorDuringUnsolicitedTurn (pass/fail), transcriptRetrievalUsable, decision (low-a-pass | low-b-required). US-006 is gated on decision==low-b-required; otherwise it is recorded skipped-with-evidence, and may instead be split into a separate follow-up PRD.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit a structured decision artifact from US-005 and gate US-006 on it.
